title: Supporting Register-based Addressing Modes for in-DRAM PIM ISAs
problem: In-DRAM Processing-in-Memory architectures incur two critical overheads: PIM code offloading to memory and data transfers between CPU and memory, limiting speedup potential for DNN inference despite eliminating compute-memory bottleneck.
motivation: PIM promises to alleviate data movement bottleneck for DNN workloads, but offloading and data transfer overhead reduce practical speedup, motivating need to reduce these control/communication costs.
method: The solution adds two new ways to specify memory addresses in processor-memory instructions: indexed addressing (combining a base address with a register value) and base-offset addressing (combining a base address with a constant offset). These methods reduce the size and complexity of each instruction because they avoid repeating full addresses. By making instructions more efficient, the system reduces the amount of data transferred between the processor and memory, and decreases the code overhead for memory operations.
key_novelty: This is the first system to support register-based addressing modes in Direct Memory Access-based in-DRAM processing-in-memory, achieving 1.94x speedup with minimal chip area and power overhead.
contributions: Indexed addressing mode for efficient register-based PIM memory access.
Base-offset addressing mode reducing CPU-PIM data transfer overhead.
1.94x speedup vs baseline PIM with only 4.65% area and 8.61% power increase.
primary_theme: register-based addressing for in-DRAM PIM acceleration
